container-office-cabin.h2: Explore every Container Office Cabin size & its applications
container-office-cabin.guidanceLine: Team figures are layout guidance from standard workstation plans — your approved drawing fixes the exact seating.

10x10.h2: 10×10 ft — the smallest cabin-form container office
10x10.intro: The smallest container office cabin puts a desk, a file rack and a visitor chair into 100 sq ft of steel-shelled workspace at the lowest entry price in our container range. It is built cabin-style — welded MS frame, insulated walls, finished interior — in the squared container form that sits neatly beside stacked site infrastructure. One supervisor runs a gate, a yard or a weighbridge from it comfortably. If your team will cross three people during the project, the 20×8 and 20×10 add floor at a lower rate per square foot.

20x8.h2: 20×8 ft — the slim value unit for gate-line duty
20x8.intro: A slim 160 sq ft unit that runs along a compound wall or gate line where a full-width office cannot sit. Three to four workstations fit in a row, and the door position is set on the approved drawing to face the traffic you manage. Yards, weighbridges and dispatch gates use it as the billing and entry-control point. The cabin-form build keeps it the most affordable slim container office we make — the premium ISO conversion of this footprint costs roughly a third more. Repeat orders along one boundary are common — the units line up door-to-door.

20x10.h2: 20×10 ft — the value benchmark of the container range
20x10.intro: The benchmark of the value line: 200 sq ft at ₹1,250 per square foot, the lowest reference rate in our container office range. Four to six people work in an open row, or three desks pair with a partitioned cabin on the drawing. It carries the same electricals, AC provision and insulation as every SAMAN unit — the saving comes from the cabin-form shell, not from the fit-out. Compare it against the converted ISO unit at this size to see exactly what the marine-grade shell adds and whether your site needs it.

20x12.h2: 20×12 ft — width for a manager bay on a budget
20x12.intro: Two extra feet of width turn a desk row into a planned office: a manager bay, a records wall or a small meeting table fits alongside five to seven workstations in 240 sq ft. Client-facing sites pick this size when meetings happen at the gate but the budget stays tight. The width rides on the same value rate band, so the step up from the 20×10 costs ₹38,000 — the least expensive way in this cluster to add a second working zone to a single unit. The manager bay takes a standard desk and two chairs; the drawing fixes its wall before fabrication.

30x10.h2: 30×10 ft — two rooms at the cluster's lowest rate
30x10.intro: A 300 sq ft long plan that partitions into a work area and a private room — the two-room layout at the lowest rate it is available anywhere in our container range. Six to eight people run daily operations while reviews happen behind the partition. The 30 ft body still travels as one unit on a standard trailer, so the two-room function arrives in a single delivery. Choose it when you need a working headquarters but the project budget was fixed before the office was. The partition position is set on your drawing, so the room split matches the team, not a template.

40x8.h2: 40×8 ft — the linear row unit for tight sites
40x8.intro: The corridor plan in cabin form: 320 sq ft as one long workstation row for sites that line their units along a boundary or between structures. Seven to nine people work in line, and repeated units make a tidy administrative row with doors aligned on the drawing. Linear infrastructure jobs use it where depth is unavailable and budgets are watched. At ₹1,175 per square foot it is the cheapest way we offer to seat a full row of staff in container form. Windows fall between workstation positions, so every desk gets daylight without glare on screens.

20x20.h2: 20×20 ft — the square floor at cabin pricing
20x20.intro: The square alternative at the same 400 sq ft and the same price as the 40×10 — the decision is purely the shape of your plot and your seating plan. Cluster desks work around the open centre, supervision lines stay short, and the middle of the floor stays free for boards or briefing. Check that the approach road takes a 20 ft wide movement before you order. Open-plan teams that found corridor offices inefficient pick this floor most often in the value line. Power and data points ring the perimeter, so cluster layouts rearrange without rewiring anything.

40x10.h2: 40×10 ft — the large-floor pick of the value line
40x10.intro: Four hundred square feet in one lift, planned into departments with a reception point at the door — the large-floor pick of the value line. Eight to twelve people work comfortably, with partitions set before fabrication. It suits offices that need headquarters scale without headquarters spend: the same floor in the ISO conversion costs about ₹2 lakh more. If the office will outlive several projects and travel between them, weigh that premium against this unit's price advantage. Reception, records and cabin walls are all positioned on the approved drawing before steel is cut.

40x12.h2: 40×12 ft — the biggest floor at the smallest rate
40x12.intro: Our largest value-line floor: 480 sq ft that partitions into cabins, a meeting room and stores, delivered complete as a single unit. Ten to fourteen people run a full site administration from it, and at ₹1,150 per square foot it carries the lowest rate of any container office we sell. It is the size where the value line makes its strongest case — maximum floor, minimum rate, one delivery. Larger requirements move to joined multi-unit layouts, quoted to drawing. The pantry point and server position are marked on the drawing alongside the cabin walls.
